arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

For integers with , we construct a uniformly quasiregular map of of degree whose Julia set is a Cantor set of concentric round spheres. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a uniformly quasiregular map in dimension three with infinitely many Fatou components. The map is a three-dimensional analogue of McMullen's maps , built from two Zorich-type power maps glued across a single shell by a slit construction. Its Julia set has Hausdorff dimension , where , and the restriction of the map to its Julia set is a skew product over the shift on two symbols and has topological entropy . We also prove that uniformly quasiregular maps that expand uniformly near their Julia set, possibly with branching there, have no wandering domains and only finitely many periodic Fatou components, all of them attracting basins. The map constructed here belongs to this class.

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

We construct infinite words whose complexity functions are quadratically bounded, but whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, resolving a question of Cassaigne. Moreover, we construct infinite words of polynomially bounded complexity, and subshifts of quasi-linear complexity, whose discrete derivatives do not decay compared to their complexity functions, thus exhibiting a typical exponentially-growing behavior. As an application, we give the first examples of subshifts of polynomial complexity whose Rauzy graphs do not have Benjamini-Schramm limits. Finally, we realize (up to an inevitable linear error factor) every function satisfying the necessary conditions, as the complexity function of a minimal, uniquely ergodic, cube-free subshift, strengthening previous realization results in this direction, and derive consequences for the growth of simple algebras and just-infinite semigroups satisfying nontrivial laws.

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

We study the Hausdorff dimension of proximal planar self-affine sets whose defining maps have diagonal or anti-diagonal linear parts, with both types present. Such systems are irreducible but not strongly irreducible. Under a projective exponential separation condition, we show that the Hausdorff dimension equals the minimum of and the affinity dimension, thereby extending the dimension formula of Hochman–Rapaport to all proximal irreducible planar systems. When the affinity dimension is at most an explicit threshold determined by the Lyapunov exponents, the formula holds assuming only that there are no exact overlaps. Above the threshold, it holds under the strong open set condition. These dimension formulae are proved by approximation with finite diagonal subsystems. Assuming projective exponential separation, we also determine the pointwise dimensions of the coordinate projections of the equilibrium state. Below the threshold, the projections are not exact-dimensional: the pointwise dimension of each exists almost everywhere and takes exactly two values, each on a set of positive measure. At or above the threshold, both projections are exact-dimensional with dimension one.

Original abstract

We investigate the structural mechanisms governing -nice and -nice recurrence in measure-preserving dynamical systems. For weakly mixing systems, we establish a complete spectral characterization of two-sided -nice recurrence via quadratic spectral functionals and Herglotz–Bochner duality, extending the theory to arbitrary integer polynomial configurations with zero constant term and to actions of countable abelian groups. Using stationary Gaussian processes and Hermite mode decoupling, we construct explicit weakly mixing counterexamples separating one-sided and two-sided -nice recurrence. Furthermore, we uncover a fundamental structural phase transition at : while recurrence is rigidly controlled by a quadratic spectral functional whose two-sided symmetrization eliminates all higher-degree cumulants, at fourth-order centered correlations survive symmetrization and can drive a strict recurrence deficit even when the quadratic spectral functional remains strictly positive. Using lacunary and multi-frequency Riesz products alongside uniform Wiener lemmas, we analyze the upper Banach density obstructions of negative spectral sets, establish partial partition regularity on the spectral cone, resolve an inverse Furstenberg correspondence problem of Rodríguez Martín for countable groups via Bernoulli product extensions, and characterize spectral -nice ultrafilters in the Stone–Čech compactification . Original abstract

In this work we extend the concept of Hecke algebras to a pair of a separable infinite profinite group and a closed core-free subgroup. Motivated by applications to minimal equicontinuous Cantor actions, which are characterized by such pairs, we characterize isometric *-algebra isomorphisms between such Hecke algebras by showing that they always arise as Koopman operators of homeomorphisms between the double coset spaces combined with the multiplication by some character. We then prove that two minimal equicontinuous Cantor actions with isometric isomorphic Hecke algebras have the same Steinitz order. We provide examples including the infinite dihedral group and the Grigorchuk group.

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

Many non-equilibrium systems, such as expanding plasmas, evolve by equations that depend explicitly on time and interpolate between autonomous early-time (UV) and late-time (IR) limits. After time is compactified, fixed points lie on invariant boundary fibers, where the Conley index is one-sided and blind to the UV. For time dependence that admits a compactification, we reflect the extended phase space across these fibers. Both sheets of the double run from the UV to the IR, and the UV index reappears, suspended by one degree. Extending one sheet slightly beyond both fibers gives an explicit UV-to-IR transport map between the Conley indices of the limit systems, and its non-vanishing forces connecting solutions. If one block with a fixed strict entrance/exit decomposition serves every frozen system, this map is an isomorphism at every admissible rate. If the block also has nonzero relative homology, the isolated invariant sets of the two limits are connected at every rate. In the Gubser flow of Israel-Stewart theory, the separatrix between two classes of initial data is a transversal connection at every finite relaxation scale , with splitting . In the Bjorken flow at the lowest moment truncation, we prove existence and uniqueness of the attractor solution without regularization. For the three-dimensional Gubser system we construct the global Morse decomposition. In the one-loop flow of the -dimensional model with cubic anisotropy, a shift of through has vanishing transport map, but a driven connection and a nonzero connecting homomorphism detect it at every rate.

Original abstract

We classify all the fixed points for the action of the pure mapping class group on character varieties of surface groups. Up to trivial peripheral monodromies, we prove that the irreducible fixed points are either pair of pants representations, or restrictions of reduced Burau representations to a once-punctured torus and restrictions of reduced Gassner representations to a 4-punctured sphere. On the other hand, we prove that the only non-trivial reducible fixed points appear in genus 0 where they map all but at most three peripheral loops in the centralizer of the image, and in genus 1 where they are valued in the quaternion group . As consequences, we deduce (i) that an irreducible representation in genus 0 with at least four non-trivial peripheral monodromies is rigid if and only if it is a fixed point, and (ii) a partial classification of irreducible representations of pure braid groups into .

Original abstract

We study the canonical skew-binary representation of nonnegative integers, whose positional weights are the Mersenne numbers , and its decomposition into the binary and nonbinary sides. The nonbinary values, arranged in increasing order, form the OEIS sequence A055938, and their successor structure gives a direct proof of the relation with the OEIS sequence A080578 that is recorded as conjectural in the OEIS entry for A080578. The resulting formulas show that the Conolly sequence describes both sides of the decomposition: a shifted Conolly sequence is the counting function of the binary side, while the same sequence gives the increasing enumeration of the nonbinary side. We then develop the parent map, truncation blocks, truncation remainders, and the Mersenne tau function associated with this representation. The parent map is conjugate to deletion of the lowest digit. Differences of the Mersenne tau rows recover the parent iterates and the counting function, and they give formulas for digit reconstruction and for a diagonal tau defect. Finally, we revisit a known finite-depth one-soliton family of the finite-field BBS. The Mersenne combinatorics is used directly to reconstruct a global integer-valued traveling-wave profile and to prove an integer window-counting theorem. Reduction modulo yields the corresponding finite-field traveling-wave solutions. We also construct an integer-valued traveling-wave tau function whose front values are given by the Mersenne tau rows. The resulting construction shows how the combinatorics of a number representation can enter directly into the reconstruction of solutions of an integrable system.

Original abstract

We extend the KAM theory for one dimensional Frenkel-Kontorova model to multidimensional case in quasi-periodic media. By using the quasi-Newton method, we reduce the linearized operator with quasi-periodic coefficient in the Nash-Moser iteration to the composition of two diagonal operators and a near-identity operator, such that the small divisor problem can be overcome by imposing the simultaneous Diophantine condition. In contrast, we also discuss the application of Craig-Wayne-Bourgain method to the quasi-periodic equilibrium problem.

Original abstract

We consider affine stochastic recursions in , where are i.i.d. in with strongly irreducible and proximal linear part. In the critical regime where the top Lyapunov exponent vanishes, we show that the recursion is locally contractive in every direction, yielding uniqueness, up to a positive multiplicative constant, of the -invariant non-zero Radon measure. This extends to every dimension a result of Babillot-Bougerol-Élie (1997) in dimension one. The proof is based on the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the "joint process" , using geometric and measure-theoretic properties of the diagonal affine action. A key ingredient is an abstract criterion for the total dissipativity of semigroup actions, which we apply to this process.

Original abstract

We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio . As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.

Original abstract

We establish a canonical topological lifting of Mundici equivalence, representing every topological MV-algebra as the unit interval of a topological -group and extending the correspondence to a categorical adjunction. As applications, we give a direct group-theoretic proof of the equivalence of and and show that every topological MV-algebra is a retral space. We further extend the lifting to topological Riesz MV-algebras and identify the canonical topology with Wiweger's mixed topology under suitable assumptions, recovering the strict topology as a special case. Finally, we obtain a unit-interval formulation of Koopman representations for continuous-time dynamical systems.

Original abstract

Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions.

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

Ample empirical evidence in deep neural network training suggests that a variety of optimizers tend to find nearly global optima. In this article, we adopt the reversed perspective that convergence to an arbitrary point is assumed rather than proven, focusing on the consequences of this assumption. From this viewpoint, in line with recent advances on the edge-of-stability phenomenon, we argue that different optimizers effectively act as eigenvalue filters determined by their hyperparameters. Specifically, the standard gradient descent method inherently avoids the sharpest minima, whereas Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) algorithms go even further by actively favoring wider basins. Inspired by these insights, we propose two novel algorithms that exhibit enhanced eigenvalue filtering, effectively promoting wider minima. Our theoretical analysis leverages a generalized Hadamard–Perron stable manifold theorem and applies to general semialgebraic functions, without requiring additional non-degeneracy conditions or global Lipschitz bound assumptions. We support our conclusions with numerical experiments on feed-forward neural networks.

Original abstract

Berry and Tabor conjectured in 1977 that spectra of generic integrable quantum systems have the same local statistics as a Poisson point process. We verify their conjecture in the case of the two-point spectral density for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box, subject to a Diophantine condition on the domain's proportions. A permissible choice of width, height and depth is for example . This extends previous work of Eskin, Margulis and Mozes (Annals of Math., 2005) in dimension two, where the problem reduces to the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for quadratic forms of signature . The difficulty in three and higher dimensions is that we need to consider the distribution of indefinite forms in shrinking rather than fixed intervals, which we are able to resolve for special diagonal forms of signature in various scalings, including a rate of convergence. A key step of our approach is to represent the relevant counting problem as an average of a theta function on over an expanding family of one-parameter unipotent orbits. The asymptotic behaviour of these unipotent averages follows from Ratner's measure classification theorem and subtle escape of mass estimates.

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

In this paper, we present a Koopman autoencoder-based least-squares policy iteration (KAE-LSPI) algorithm for reinforcement learning (RL). The KAE-LSPI algorithm is based on reformulating the so-called least-squares fixed-point approximation method in terms of extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD), thereby enabling automatic feature learning via the Koopman autoencoder (KAE) framework. The approach is motivated by the lack of a systematic procedure for selecting features or kernels in linear RL techniques. Unlike previous approaches, no features or kernels need to be fixed a priori in our method. We discuss the theoretical convergence of KAE-LSPI under suitable assumptions, similar to kernel-based least-squares policy iteration (KLSPI). We empirically compare our method with two existing algorithms: least-squares policy iteration (LSPI) and KLSPI. In particular, for the chainwalk problem, the resulting policies are either optimal or nearly optimal for both three approaches. For the cart-pole system, KAE-LSPI outperforms the other two approaches in terms of policy performance.
